name: Gallim
title: Levitical singer in the temple
summary: Gallim was a Levite who served as a singer in the temple after returning from the Babylonian exile. He is mentioned in the genealogies of 1 Chronicles and Nehemiah as part of the Levites who settled in Jerusalem and resumed temple service. His role testifies to the restoration of God's worship after the exile.

keyEvents.title: Listed among the Levites in Jerusalem
keyEvents.description: Gallim is mentioned among the Levites who settled in Jerusalem after returning from Babylon, as part of the restoration of temple service.

keyEvents.title: Serving in the temple
keyEvents.description: As a descendant of Jeduthun, Gallim participated in the Levitical singing service in the temple, an important part of worship in the rebuilt temple.

keyEvents.title: Mentioned in Nehemiah's genealogy
keyEvents.description: Gallim is also mentioned in the book of Nehemiah among the Levites who helped restore religious order in Jerusalem after the exile.

keyEvents.title: Part of the restored community
keyEvents.description: Galal was part of the larger community of priests, Levites, and temple workers who ensured that God's worship was restored in accordance with the Law of Moses after the exile.
